summary.short: Commission decisions of 25 April 2023 and 26 April 2024 designating named online platforms and search engines as very large under Article 33(4) of the Digital Services Act, each addressed to named provider entities, based on reported average monthly active recipients above 45 million in the Union.
summary.long: Bundle of Commission decisions under Article 33(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act). Nineteen decisions of 25 April 2023 designate AliExpress, Bing, TikTok, App Store, Facebook, Booking.com, Google Maps, LinkedIn, Google Play, Google Shopping, Instagram, Snapchat, Amazon Store, Google Search, Twitter, Pinterest, Wikipedia, YouTube and Zalando as very large online platforms or, for Bing and Google Search, very large online search engines. A decision of 26 April 2024 designates SHEIN. Each rests on reported average monthly active recipients in the Union above 45 million. Article 1 of each decision makes the designation; Article 2 names the addressee, usually a subsidiary or main establishment in the Union, or a non-EU entity where none exists (Snapchat, Wikipedia). The SHEIN decision states that only the SHEIN Marketplace service is subject to the Regulation's obligations. A corrigendum of 13 July 2023 corrects recital numbering and a service name in the Google Search decision.

relations.note: Each of the 20 designation decisions cites Article 33(4) as the power under which the Commission designates an online platform or online search engine as very large; the designation threshold is stated in Article 33(1) of the same regulation.

notes: The document compiles 20 Commission decisions of 25.4.2023 (one of them, SHEIN, dated 26.4.2024 and marked DOWNGRADED ON 15.5.2024, /2 version) plus a corrigendum of 13.7.2023 (C(2023) 4883) to the Google Search decision, which corrects recital (4) (Google Play to Google Search) and renumbers recitals. Internal inconsistencies: the SHEIN addressee is 'Infinite Styles Services Co.' in the recitals but 'Infinite Style Services, Ltd' in Art. 2; the Google Search recital (4) cites 'Regulation (EU) 2022/206'; the Booking.com recital (4) refers to 'BIH' where BHI is meant; the Snapchat decision cites 'Regulation 2022/2065' without EU. Several decisions state that the Commission cannot exclude that parent or group entities (e.g. Alibaba Group, Microsoft Corp., Alphabet, Meta Inc., Apple Inc.) also provide the service, and do not resolve this. Entities list addressees only; Member States consulted and the Commission are not listed. Lei and ticker are not verified and left empty. Only English text is authentic.

thresholds.variable_text: average monthly active recipients in the Union
thresholds.value_text: an online platform which has a number of average monthly active recipients in the Union equal to or higher than 45 million
thresholds.measurement: Average monthly active recipients in the Union in the period preceding the provider's publication, as reported by the provider under Art. 24(2) or available to the Commission; the Commission decides on that basis
thresholds.consequence: The Commission designates the online platform or online search engine as a very large online platform or very large online search engine.
thresholds.conditions: Applies to online platforms and online search engines; decision taken after consulting the Member State of establishment or taking into account the Digital Services Coordinator's information (Art. 33(4)).

evidence.quote: an online platform which has a number of average monthly active recipients in the Union equal to or higher than 45 million
It is therefore an online platform within the meaning of Article 3, point (i), of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065.
It is therefore an online search engine within the meaning of Article 3, point (j), of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065.
AliExpress should be designated as a very large online platform within the meaning of Article 33(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065.
AliExpress is a hosting service within the meaning of Article 3, point (g)(iii), of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
Bing is an intermediary service within the meaning of Article 3, point (g), of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065

Article 3, point (b), of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 defines ‘recipient of the service’ as ‘any natural or legal person who uses an intermediary service, in particular for the purposes of seeking information or making it accessible’.

definitions.term: active recipient of an online platform

evidence.quote: Article 3, point (p), of that Regulation defines ‘active recipient of an online platform’ as ‘a recipient of the service that has engaged with an online platform by either requesting the online platform to host information or being exposed to information hosted by the online platform and disseminated through its online interface’.

obligations.note: Each decision's operative provisions (Article 1 designates the named service as a very large online platform or search engine under Regulation (EU) 2022/2065; Article 2 names the addressee entity) impose no new duty on any addressee. Obligations of designated providers arise under Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, which the decisions cite (e.g., Article 24(2), Article 33(4)) but do not reproduce or re-impose. Recitals that describe the consequences of designation are context only and are not coded.

enforcement.note: The document is a set of Commission decisions designating platforms and search engines as very large under Article 33(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065. It contains no sanction, fine, penalty, revocation, suspension or blocking provisions, and cites no enforcement provisions as operative.
